author: Santanu Sardal
text:
⭐ **Iconic Landmark of Delhi

I recently visited **India Gate** and it was a wonderful experience. This historic war memorial stands proudly in the heart of **New Delhi** and honors the soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the country.

The atmosphere around the monument is lively, especially in the evening when the lights make it look even more beautiful. Families, tourists, and locals come here to relax, take photos, and enjoy the open surroundings.

Nearby you can also see **Amar Jawan Jyoti**, which adds a strong patriotic feeling to the visit.

Overall, it is a must-visit place in Delhi for history lovers, tourists, and anyone who wants to experience the pride of India. 🇮🇳

author: Yash Manjrekar
text:
The atmosphere here is really cool. You get a sense of pride here.. The area has been kept very clean and gives good vibes. The underground passages are very helpful in crossing the roads.

The food court is pretty good as well providing many different cuisines. The concept of having outlets of different States providing cuisines of their particular States embodies the essence of India perfectly.

author: Akhil Rai
text:
I had the chance to visit India Gate and it felt really amazing. 🇮🇳
The environment there is very peaceful and beautiful. People enjoy their time with family and friends. Seeing India Gate gives a special feeling in the heart because it is built in memory of the brave soldiers of our country.

In the evening, with the lights on, India Gate looks even more beautiful. Standing there made me feel proud of my country.

If you are in Delhi, you should definitely visit India Gate at least once. This place gives peace to the heart and increases respect for the nation. ❤️

author: Kaushik Patra
text:
Visited India Gate recently and it’s truly one of those places that feels bigger than just a monument. 🇮🇳
Standing in front of it, especially in the evening when it’s beautifully lit, gives you a sense of pride and calm at the same time. The architecture is grand yet simple, and knowing it’s a tribute to Indian soldiers makes the experience even more meaningful.

Tip: Visit after sunset for the best vibe, and try going on a weekday to avoid heavy crowds.

author: Oscar Berto
text: A truly iconic and majestic monument. Visiting it at night is a magical experience; the lighting on the arch and the nearby fountains is spectacular. Be prepared for many locals who will ask to take photos with you with the Gate in the background, and many tuk-tuk drivers offering rides. My advice is to use Uber for more reliable and transparent transport. A must-see in Delhi

author: Ram
text:
India Gate is one of Delhi’s most iconic landmarks and a powerful war memorial. The structure is impressive up close, especially in the evening when it’s beautifully lit. The Amar Jawan Jyoti adds emotional significance and makes the visit more meaningful.
The surrounding lawns are well-maintained and great for a relaxed walk or sitting with friends and family. It can get quite crowded, particularly on weekends, and there are many street vendors around, but the overall atmosphere is lively and enjoyable.
Best time to visit is around sunset for cooler weather and better views.
A must-visit spot in Delhi at least once.

author: Sonpi
text: A quiet sorroundings right at the heart of Delhi, India Gate and its premises offer valuable wind down location. Just hang out with friends or family while enjoying the view of this awesome monument. If you go after dark you get to see the monument lighted up with the tiranga colours. Just beware of the cameramen and auto rickshaw drivers. They are out there to squeeze out any advantages from tourists.

author: Bendalam Sai Chanikya
text: “India Gate is absolutely beautiful and full of history. The monument feels majestic and the surrounding park is peaceful and well‑maintained. A must‑visit place in Delhi to feel pride in our soldiers’ sacrifice.”

author: Jow Salik
text:
The India Gate is best experienced early in the morning. We arrived just after 8:00 AM, and it was surprisingly cold, which made the walk around the area even more refreshing.

The gardens surrounding the monument are beautifully maintained, with fountains adding to the calm atmosphere. Seeing India Gate up close really puts its scale into perspective—it’s massive and impressive in real life.

Coming early is highly recommended to avoid the crowds and fully enjoy the space at a relaxed pace. There’s no entrance fee, making it an easy and worthwhile stop on any Delhi itinerary.
